A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same JanusDNA research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v3 reports original JanusDNA training-efficiency experiments, results on three genomic benchmarks, and MoE/mid-attention ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds reverse-complement, causal-model, and MLP experiments, plus mouse transcription-factor binding results.

M1.justification: Appendix B.1.4 introduces JanusDNA-MLP by adding an MLP after the feature-fusion attention module. The original bidirectional encoders, pretraining objective, attention mask, MoE design, and reverse-complement strategy remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v4 adds GUE mouse transcription-factor binding prediction across five categories (Table 12) and middle-token prediction evaluation (Table 7). HG38 pretraining and the original three benchmarks remain. This extends genomic task coverage; mouse evaluation was already present through the Genomic Benchmark.

E2.justification: ConvNova enters Tables 1–2, while the Mamba NTP comparator disappears from Table 1. Appendix B.1.3 adds parameter-matched causal models to the training-paradigm comparisons. The new mouse comparison also includes DNABERT k-mer models and additional Nucleotide Transformer variants absent from v3's reported comparisons, substantially broadening the comparator set.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 changes Janus's stated evaluation input from the first T−1 tokens to the full sequence with the last token masked; the retained accuracy figure does not establish that evaluation was rerun. Added studies introduce parameter-matched causal controls, a fixed-setting five-fold RC evaluation, and mouse fine-tuning for 10 epochs with batch size 32 and learning rate 1e-3. Main benchmark configurations also switch to slightly larger MLP variants.

E4.justification: Appendices B.1.2–B.1.4 add substantial component and mechanism tests: RC inclusion across task types, Janus versus causal modeling for last- and middle-token prediction, and post-fusion MLP ablations on NT and eQTL tasks. The earlier MoE and mid-attention analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: New Table 5 reports standard deviations across five CV seeds for the RC ablation. Existing benchmark reporting of ranges across five or ten seeds, and the single-run eQTL protocol, remain unchanged. This adds an uncertainty-reporting practice without establishing increased replication of existing experiments.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 report new MLP and ConvNova results. Original NT Janus scores are retained exactly in v4 Table 8, while Table 3 retains original eQTL scores and adds MLP results, including adipose AUROC 0.769 versus the original variant's 0.741. The MLP variant leads all nine eQTL datasets. Updated Tables 1–2 show Janus leading 2/8 and 11/18 tasks, versus 3/8 and 12/18 previously, under changed model/comparator configurations. RC, causal, middle-token, and mouse results further expand the findings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9, including the Janus objective, fusion mask, and MoE auxiliary loss, are unchanged. Neither version's appendices introduce additional formal results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient bidirectional pretraining, the hybrid architecture, million-base-pair processing, and parameter-efficient benchmark performance. The added experiments are not recast as new core contributions.

C2.justification: v4 qualifies RC's previously described general benefits by explaining its adverse effects on strand-specific splice-site prediction. It interprets the causal comparisons as evidence of richer representations and the mouse results as generalization from human-only pretraining. The conclusion's existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 specifies that RC representations are averaged only during inference, clarifies full-model eQTL fine-tuning, and documents the causal comparator architecture and new RC/mouse experiment settings. Existing pretraining tables, hardware disclosures, and code/checkpoint access information are retained.

R1.justification: Three biological references—Schulz et al., Wei et al., and Mikhaylichenko et al.—support expanded introductory discussion of bidirectional promoters and enhancers. Appendix A's model review and the central novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The appendix is reorganized from separate C–E sections into B.1–B.3, with additional subsections for new analyses. Existing prose is largely retained, alongside localized introduction and terminology edits and an added funding acknowledgment.

P2.justification: Result presentation expands substantially through new RC, causal-prediction, MLP, and mouse-comparison tables and revised model/comparator columns in Tables 1–3. Original NT results are redisplayed alongside MLP variants. All six figure graphics are retained; Figures 3–4 exchange numbering and placement, Figure 6 moves, and the efficiency caption gains a legend clarification.

improvement.justification: The added causal, RC, and MLP controls strengthen empirical support and reveal a useful strand-specific limitation; ConvNova and mouse comparisons broaden validation. These benefits are tempered by reporting inconsistencies: the text retains 3/8 and 12/18 wins although revised Tables 1–2 show 2/8 and 11/18, and Table 5's caption reverses its mid-attention column-group descriptions. Overall, the evidence improves, but presentation and reporting weaknesses limit the net gain.
